rv.q: Cole Escola’s Oh, Mary! is not just funny: It is dizzyingly, breathtakingly funny, the kind of funny that ambushes your body into uncontained laughter.
Oh, Mary! is hilarious and, underneath the mayhem, both structurally rock solid and sneakily moving.

With nods and hints to Charles Busch, the late, great and forever Ridiculous Everett Quinton, the Sedaris siblings, Carol Burnett, Pee-wee Herman and Absolutely Fabulous, Escola squeezes just enough juice from their influences for a mix that is entirely fresh and not to be missed.
And yet the Great White Way has not witnessed a comedy this funny, or a comedic star turn this dazzling, in at least a decade.
The play itself is a masterclass in comedy, relying on the impeccable timing of the actors to keep each joke perfectly in tune with the audience.
Rather, the play, which opened on Thursday at the Lyceum Theater, is one of the best crafted and most exactingly directed Broadway comedies in years.
Cole Escola's irreverent comedy reimagines Mary Todd Lincoln as a boozy, foul-mouthed misfit desperate to escape the White House for a career on the stage.
Oh, Mary! is a work of deranged beauty: a version of Mary Todd Lincoln told through the lens of an idiot, played with all the verve and severity of Bette Davis on bath salts.
Escola’s splendidly nasty queer romp has hiked up its petticoats and staggered uptown from a sold-out run at the Theatre, goosing a sleepy Broadway summer.
Point of fact, pretty much everything in this show is hilarious.
Escola’s coup – the real liberation of the play – is to bring us so close to Mary’s white-hot rage, lust and delusion that we can’t help but root for her.
'Oh, Mary!' is directed by Sam Pinkleton at a breakneck speed that both allows room for the best jokes to harvest their share of laughter while never letting even the lesser gags land with a thud.
The runaway First Family spoof continues its agenda of delirious, deranged and undeniable fun on Broadway.
The show is a sendup of both Lincoln and his wife, Mary Todd Lincoln, reimagined as a foul-mouthed, alcoholic aspiring cabaret star who feels trapped by her role as First Lady.
What a relief that in its West End form, Oh, Mary! remains just as outrageous, hysterically funny and genuinely unpredictable as its Broadway counterpart.

The delights of Oh, Mary! (Lyceum Theater, booking to Sept 15) are many, varied, and all-winning. If, like many, the world and life in general has left you tense, this Broadway show—transferred by way of rave reviews and celebrity visitors from an award-laden sold-out run at the Theat...
Yes, the future of Broadway is here and it’s Cole Escola’s stupid masterpiece Oh, Mary!
Do yourself a favor. Join the cult.
The entire ensemble elevates very silly jokes into a work of art that keeps you riveted from start to finish.
It is, without a doubt, the funniest comedy on Broadway right now.
Escola’s brilliant lunacy is the real deal.
Experiencing this comedy with a few hundred more theatergoers takes the laughter from boisterous to atomic and the effect is absolutely radioactive.
Oh, Mary! is laugh-out-loud funny from the first moments; though much of the humor comes from Escola’s unbelievable delivery and the slapstick combination of actors on stage.

Cole Escola, who has tackled a variety of boldface characters on stage and television, manages to sustain a delirious fit of pique through most of the show’s 80 minutes without losing our attention for even a moment; this Mary would approve.
What makes Mary so wickedly delicious to watch and listen to is that she does precisely what is in bad taste and against all the rules of polite society.

The script, and the direction of Sam Pinkleton (erstwhile choreographer of Natasha, Pierre & the Great Comet of 1812), start things off at too high a level that eventually leads to some lulls. And Mary’s character arc, while necessarily schizophrenic, could be laid out more cleanly.
I was too busy admiring the script and every element of this production.
So, what if you don’t find this alternative history all that funny?
Elder viewers reared on the comparatively subtle writing and performance style of Charles Busch are likely to find Escola’s slapdash artistry crude, but there’s no denying he snags laughs.
Oh, Mary! on Broadway was possibly the most fun I’ve had in a theater ever in my life— a compliment I don’t give lightly.
One of the funniest shows of the year, Oh, Mary! is the perfect antidote in the season to feel jolly.

Mary’s Husband has a teacher (Dino Fetscher of The Normal Heart ) come in and share the works of Shakespeare, including The Tempest (no, not that one ). Escola’s script establishes Mary as an utter diva through one perfect motif, which is that the protagonist puts on the most melodramatic displays of effort for the most minor of outcomes.
This is a cheerful night of theater (including a raucous finale), especially if you’re on Escola’s wacky yet endearing wavelength.
It is one of the funniest shows one will ever get to see on stage.

cn.t: Critics hail Cole Escola's irreverent farce as howlingly funny, with most praising its absurdist take on Mary Todd Lincoln as a boozy, cabaret-obsessed diva. While a few find it too niche or messy, the consensus celebrates its campy brilliance and non-stop laughs.
